Kriukai Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiauliai County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Kriukai was the birthplace of Hillel Kook, a Revisionist Zionist activist who worked in the United States during WWII to promote Zionism and raise awareness of the Holocaust, later serving in Israel's first Knesset; he was a nephew of Rabbi Abraham Isaac Kook, the first Chief Rabbi of the future State of Israel. The village's Jewish community, established in the early 19th century, traded in flax, grains, fruit, and livestock with local peasants and across the border in Latvia's Courland province. On Yom Kippur 1941, all of Kriukai's remaining Jews were murdered in Naryshkin Park alongside the Jews of nearby Žagarė. This cemetery, dating to the same period as the community's founding, was left undisturbed during the Soviet era.
